subject: How can I get intercept results?

messages.author: 01a10202e22a9666
messages.subject: How can I get intercept results?
parts:
Dear Lavaan researcher,
I;m trying to analyze LGM(Latent Growth Curve Model) with correaltion matrix. After calculation I can't get the result of Intercepts. So I don't make estimate equation.The followings are syntax and the result of parts. Of course I got average of variables(2.271, 2.560, 2.694, 2.965, 0.573, 0.554).
Thanks a lot in advance.
Best regards. 
 
[syntax]
library(lavaan)
library(semPlot)
Bagcor.str<-'
1.000
0.640   1.000
0.586   0.670   1.000
0.454   0.566   0.621   1.000
0.001   0.038   0.118   0.091   1.000
-0.214 -0.149   -0.135   -0.163 -0.025   1.000'
varnames<-c("y1", "y2", "y3", "y4", "gender","income")
Bagcor<-getCov(Bagcor.str,names=varnames)
round(Bagcor,4)
Bag.model<-'
# intercept and slope
# with fixed coefficients
i =~ 1*y1 + 1*y2 + 1*y3 + 1*y4
s =~ 0*y1 + 1*y2 + 2*y3 + 3*y4
# regressions
i ~ gender + income
s ~ gender + income'
round(Bagcor,4)
Bag.out1<-growth(Bag.model,sample.cov = Bagcor,sample.nobs = 321)
summary(Bag.out1)
fitmeasures(Bag.out1)
[result]
Intercepts:
                   Estimate  Std.Err  z-value  P(>|z|)
   .y1                0.000                           
   .y2                0.000                           
   .y3                0.000                           
   .y4                0.000                           
   .i                 0.000    0.053    0.000    1.000
   .s                 0.000    0.018    0.000    1.000

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: How can I get intercept results?
parts: I;m trying to analyze LGM(Latent Growth Curve Model) with correaltion matrix. After calculation I can't get the result of Intercepts.

How can lavaan estimate means if you don't tell lavaan what the observed means are?  All you supply is a correlation matrix, so it has to assume all the observed means are zero.

FYI, analyzing a correlation matrix yields incorrect SEs unless you constrain the error variances such that the total variance == 1.  You should analyze the covariance matrix instead, if have access to the SDs.  You can use in the getCov function to rescale the correlation matrix using the SDs.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: 6a75f6f91a59c568
messages.subject: Re: How can I get intercept results?
parts:
Hi,

That's hard to know how much increase mean among time variants when using correlation table. In most situations, the LGM requires the raw response/assessment dataset to solve the sample attrition (missing value) problem with multiple imputations. See the ?semTools::growth.mi.

Best wishes,

Seongho Bae
Psy.D student in Work Psychology for the large-scale assessment and measurement for high-stake personnel decisions
Industrial Psychology department, the Kwangwoon University
